verses.zh: 我自夸固然无益，但我是不得已的。如今我要说到主的显现和启示。
verses.en: It is necessary to go on boasting.[NOTE:1] Though it is not profitable, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
notes: Grk “Boasting is necessary.”

verses.zh: 我认得一个在基督里的人，他前十四年被提到第三层天上去；（或在身内，我不知道；或在身外，我也不知道；只有　神知道。）
verses.en: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago (whether in the body or out of the body I do not know, God knows) was caught up to the third heaven.

verses.zh: 我认得这人；（或在身内，或在身外，我都不知道，只有　神知道。）
verses.en: And I know that this man (whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows)

verses.zh: 他被提到乐园里，听见隐秘的言语，是人不可说的。
verses.en: was caught up into paradise[NOTE:1] and heard things too sacred to be put into words,[NOTE:2] things that a person[NOTE:3] is not permitted to speak.
notes: In the NT, paradise is mentioned three times. In Luke 23:43 it refers to the abode of the righteous dead. In Rev 2:7 it refers to the restoration of Edenic paradise predicted in Isa 51:3 and Ezek 36:35. The reference here in 2 Cor 12:4 is probably to be translated as parallel to the mention of the “third heaven” in v. 2. Assuming that the “first heaven” would be atmospheric heaven (the sky) and “second heaven” the more distant stars and planets, “third heaven” would refer to the place where God dwells. This is much more likely than some variation on the seven heavens mentioned in the pseudepigraphic book 2 Enoch and in other nonbiblical and rabbinic works.
Or “things that cannot be put into words.”
Grk “a man.”

verses.zh: 为这人，我要夸口；但是为我自己，除了我的软弱以外，我并不夸口。
verses.en: On behalf of such an individual I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except about my weaknesses.

verses.zh: 我就是愿意夸口也不算狂，因为我必说实话；只是我禁止不说，恐怕有人把我看高了，过于他在我身上所看见、所听见的。
verses.en: For even if I wish to boast, I will not be a fool, for I would be telling[NOTE:1] the truth, but I refrain from this so that no one may regard[NOTE:2] me beyond what he sees in me or what he hears from me,
notes: Or “speaking.”
Or “may think of.”

verses.zh: 又恐怕我因所得的启示甚大，就过于自高，所以有一根刺加在我肉体上，就是撒但的差役要攻击我，免得我过于自高。
verses.en: even because of the extraordinary character of the revelations. Therefore,[NOTE:1] so that I would not become arrogant, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to trouble[NOTE:2] me—so that I would not become arrogant.[NOTE:3]
notes: Most mss (P46 D Ψ 1881 M) lack διό (dio, “Therefore”), but the widespread distribution and quality of mss which include it (א A B F G 0243 33 81 1175 1739) argues for its authenticity. Internally, its case is equally strong in that its inclusion is grammatically rough (διό is hardly necessary to convey purpose, especially since Paul uses ἵνα [hina, “so that”] next).
Or “to harass.”

The phrase “so that I might not become arrogant” is repeated here because it occurs in the Greek text two times in the verse. Although redundant, it is repeated because of the emphatic nature of its affirmation.

verses.zh: 为这事，我三次求过主，叫这刺离开我。
verses.en: I asked the Lord three times about this, that it would depart from me.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「我的恩典够你用的，因为我的能力是在人的软弱上显得完全。」所以，我更喜欢夸自己的软弱，好叫基督的能力覆庇我。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] he said to me, “My grace is enough[NOTE:2] for you, for my[NOTE:3] power is made perfect[NOTE:4] in weakness.” So then, I will boast most gladly[NOTE:5] about my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may reside in[NOTE:6] me.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” because of the contrast implicit in the context.
Or “is sufficient.”

The majority of later mss (א2 Ac D1 Ψ 0243 0278 33 1739 1881 M) as well as some versional witnesses include the pronoun “my” here, but the omission of the pronoun has excellent external support (P46vid א* A* B D* F G latt). Scribes probably added the pronoun for clarity, making the obvious referent explicit. This would also make “power” more parallel with “my grace.” Though the original text probably did not include “my,” scribes who added the word were following the sense of Paul’s statement.tn The pronoun “my” was supplied in the translation to clarify the sense of Paul’s expression.
Or “my power comes to full strength.”
“Most gladly,” a comparative form used with superlative meaning and translated as such.
Or “may rest on.”

verses.zh: 我为基督的缘故，就以软弱、凌辱、急难、逼迫、困苦为可喜乐的；因我甚么时候软弱，甚么时候就刚强了。
verses.en: Therefore I am content with[NOTE:1] weaknesses, with insults, with troubles, with persecutions and difficulties[NOTE:2] for the sake of Christ, for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
notes: Or “I take delight in.”
Or “calamities.”

verses.zh: 我成了愚妄人，是被你们强逼的。我本该被你们称许才是。我虽算不了甚么，却没有一件事在那些最大的使徒以下。
verses.en: I have become a fool. You yourselves forced me to do it, for I should have been commended by you. For I lack nothing in comparison[NOTE:1] to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
notes: Or “I am in no way inferior.”

verses.zh: 我在你们中间，用百般的忍耐，藉着神迹、奇事、异能显出使徒的凭据来。
verses.en: Indeed, the signs of an apostle were performed among you with great perseverance[NOTE:1] by signs and wonders and powerful deeds.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “patience,” “endurance.”
Or “and miracles.”

verses.zh: 除了我不累着你们这一件事，你们还有甚么事不及别的教会呢？这不公之处，求你们饶恕我吧。
verses.en: For how[NOTE:1] were you treated worse than the other churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this injustice!
notes: Grk “For in what respect.”

verses.zh: 如今，我打算第三次到你们那里去，也必不累着你们；因我所求的是你们，不是你们的财物。儿女不该为父母积财，父母该为儿女积财。
verses.en: Look, for the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you, because I do not want your possessions, but you. For children should not have[NOTE:1] to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
notes: Grk “children ought not,” but this might give the impression that children are not supposed to support sick or aging parents in need of help. That is not what Paul is saying. His point is that children should not have to pay their parent’s way.

verses.zh: 我也甘心乐意为你们的灵魂费财费力。难道我越发爱你们，就越发少得你们的爱吗？
verses.en: Now I will most gladly spend and be spent for your lives![NOTE:1] If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
notes: Grk “souls.”

verses.zh: 罢了，我自己并没有累着你们，你们却有人说，我是诡诈，用心计牢笼你们。
verses.en: But be that as it may, I have not burdened you. Yet because I was a crafty person, I took you in by deceit!

verses.zh: 我所差到你们那里去的人，我藉着他们一个人占过你们的便宜吗？
verses.en: I have not taken advantage of you through anyone I have sent to you, have I?[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek construction anticipates a negative answer, indicated by the ‘tag’ question “have I?” at the end of the clause. The question is rhetorical.

verses.zh: 我劝了提多到你们那里去，又差那位兄弟与他同去。提多占过你们的便宜吗？我们行事，不同是一个心灵（或译：圣灵）吗？不同是一个脚踪吗？
verses.en: I urged Titus to visit you,[NOTE:1] and I sent our[NOTE:2] brother along with him. Titus did not take advantage of you, did he?[NOTE:3] Did we not conduct ourselves in the same spirit? Did we not behave in the same way?[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “to visit you” are not in the Greek text but are implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, and must be supplied for the modern reader.
Grk “the.”
The Greek construction anticipates a negative answer, indicated by the ‘tag’ question “did he?” at the end of the clause.

Grk “[Did we not walk] in the same tracks?” This is an idiom that means to imitate someone else or to behave as they do. Paul’s point is that he and Titus have conducted themselves in the same way toward the Corinthians. If Titus did not take advantage of the Corinthians, then neither did Paul.

verses.zh: 你们到如今，还想我们是向你们分诉；我们本是在基督里当　神面前说话。亲爱的弟兄啊，一切的事都是为造就你们。
verses.en: Have you been thinking all this time[NOTE:1] that we have been defending ourselves to you? We are speaking in Christ before God, and everything we do, dear friends, is to build you up.[NOTE:2]
notes: The reading “all this time” (πάλαι, palai) is found in several early and significant Alexandrian and Western witnesses including א* A B F G 0243 6 33 81 365 1175 1739 1881 lat; the reading πάλιν (palin, “again”) is read by א2 D Ψ 0278 M sy bo; the reading οὐ πάλαι (ou palai) is read by P46, making the question even more emphatic. The reading of P46 could only have arisen from πάλαι. The reading πάλιν is significantly easier (“are you once again thinking that we are defending ourselves?”), for it softens Paul’s tone considerably. It thus seems to be a motivated reading and cannot easily explain the rise of πάλαι. Further, πάλαι has considerable support in the Alexandrian and Western witnesses, rendering it virtually certain as the autographic wording here.
Or “for your strengthening”; Grk “for your edification.”

gr.gloss: we have been making a defense

verses.zh: 我怕我再来的时候，见你们不合我所想望的，你们见我也不合你们所想望的；又怕有纷争、嫉妒、恼怒、结党、毁谤、谗言、狂傲、混乱的事。
verses.en: For I am afraid that somehow when I come I will not find you what I wish, and you will find me[NOTE:1] not what you wish. I am afraid that[NOTE:2] somehow there may be quarreling, jealousy, intense anger, selfish ambition,[NOTE:3] slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
notes: Grk “and I will be found by you.” The passive construction has been converted to an active one in the translation.
The words “I am afraid that” are not repeated in the Greek text, but are needed for clarity.
Or “intense anger, hostility.”

verses.zh: 且怕我来的时候，我的　神叫我在你们面前惭愧，又因许多人从前犯罪，行污秽、奸淫、邪荡的事不肯悔改，我就忧愁。
verses.en: I am afraid that[NOTE:1] when I come again, my God may humiliate me before you, and I will grieve for[NOTE:2] many of those who previously sinned and have not repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and licentiousness that they have practiced.
notes: The words “I am afraid that” are not repeated in the Greek text from v. 20, but are needed for clarity.
Or “I will mourn over.”
